tables.purpose: This table records product return transactions made by customers. It captures which order and order line were returned, the return date, reason, current status, and the refund amount.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for each return record
Identifier of the original order that the return belongs to
Identifier of the specific line item in the order that is being returned
Date and time when the return was processed
Reason code supplied by the customer for the return (e.g., changed_mind, wrong_item)
Current processing state of the return (e.g., approved, refunded)
Monetary amount refunded to the customer

tables.relationships: order_id links to orders.order_id; order_item_id links to order_items.order_item_id.
tables.business_value: Enables analysis of why products are returned, how much money is refunded, and which orders or items generate the most returns.

ambiguity_flags.note: status here records the return's processing stage (approved, refunded, etc.). Other tables also have a status column (suppliers, marketing_campaigns, customers, orders, products) with different value sets such as active, completed, cancelled; there is no declared relationship, so the shared name likely refers to unrelated concepts.
refund_amount is a monetary value, but the currency (e.g., USD, EUR) is not indicated in the sample data.

tables.purpose: This table lists the companies that provide products to the business. It stores each supplier’s name, country, contact email, and current operational status.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for each supplier
Legal name of the supplier
Country where the supplier is located
Email address for contacting the supplier
Current relationship status of the supplier (e.g., active)

tables.business_value: Supports sourcing analysis, such as identifying active suppliers by country and monitoring supplier availability.

ambiguity_flags.note: status here indicates whether the supplier relationship is active. Other tables also have a status column (returns, marketing_campaigns, customers, orders, products) with different meanings like approved, completed, cancelled; no declared link suggests the same name is used generically.

country records the supplier’s location. Customers also have a country column, but the sampled values do not overlap, indicating the two columns refer to different entities (supplier location vs. customer residence) without a declared relationship.

tables.purpose: This table tracks the stock levels for each product. It records the quantity on hand, the reorder threshold, and the last time the record was updated.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for each inventory record
Identifier of the product whose stock is being tracked
Number of units of the product currently in stock
Stock level at which a new order should be placed
Timestamp of the most recent inventory count update

tables.business_value: Enables monitoring of product availability and triggers for replenishment based on stock thresholds.

tables.purpose: This table logs marketing campaigns run by the company. It tracks each campaign’s name, channel, start and end dates, budget, and current status.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for each campaign
Descriptive name of the campaign
Marketing channel used for the campaign (e.g., affiliate, social_media)
Date when the campaign began
Date when the campaign ended or null if ongoing
Planned spend for the campaign
Current state of the campaign (e.g., active, completed, paused)

tables.business_value: Allows assessment of spend effectiveness by channel and time period, and tracking of campaign lifecycles.

ambiguity_flags.note: channel here refers to marketing medium such as affiliate or social_media. Orders also have a channel column (in_store, marketplace, mobile_app, web) with no overlapping values, indicating the same name describes different concepts without a declared link.

status here indicates the campaign's lifecycle stage. Other tables (returns, suppliers, customers, orders, products) also have a status column with unrelated value sets; no declared relationship suggests a generic use of the term.
budget is a monetary amount, but the currency is not specified in the sample data.

tables.purpose: This table contains information about individual customers. It records their contact details, signup date, country, segmentation label, and account status.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for each customer
Customer's email address
Customer's given name
Customer's family name
Date when the customer created an account
Country of residence of the customer
Business-assigned customer segment (e.g., at_risk, new, regular, high_value)
Current account status (e.g., active, inactive, churned)

tables.business_value: Supports segmentation analysis to understand customer value, churn risk, and geographic distribution.

ambiguity_flags.note: status here reflects the account's condition. Other tables (returns, suppliers, marketing_campaigns, orders, products) also have a status column with different meanings; no declared link indicates the term is used generically across tables.

country records the customer's residence. Suppliers also have a country column for supplier location, but the sampled values do not overlap, suggesting the columns refer to different entities without a declared relationship.
segment categories are business-defined labels; the exact criteria for each label are not provided in the sample, making the meaning of each segment ambiguous.

tables.purpose: This table records each purchase order placed by a customer. It tracks the order’s date, sales channel, status, and total monetary amount.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for each order
Identifier of the customer who placed the order
Timestamp when the order was created
Current fulfillment state of the order (e.g., cancelled, refunded)
Sales channel through which the order was placed (e.g., in_store, marketplace, mobile_app, web)
Total monetary value of the order

tables.business_value: Enables analysis of sales volume, revenue by channel, and order fulfilment performance.

ambiguity_flags.note: status here describes the order's fulfillment stage. Other tables (returns, suppliers, marketing_campaigns, customers, products) also have a status column with unrelated value sets; no declared link suggests a generic usage.

channel here indicates where the purchase was made (in_store, marketplace, mobile_app, web). Marketing_campaigns also has a channel column (affiliate, email, paid_search, social_media) with no overlapping values, so the shared name likely refers to different concepts.
total_amount is a monetary figure, but the currency is not indicated in the sample.

tables.purpose: This table breaks down each order into its constituent line items. It records which product was ordered, the quantity, and the unit price.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for each line item
Identifier of the order to which this line item belongs
Identifier of the product being purchased
Number of units of the product in this line item
Price per unit of the product for this line item

tables.relationships: order_id links to orders.order_id; product_id links to products.product_id.
tables.business_value: Supports detailed revenue analysis per product and quantity sold per order.

ambiguity_flags.note: unit_price is a monetary amount, but the currency is not specified in the sample data.

tables.purpose: This table catalogs the products the company sells. It stores each product’s name, category, price, status, and the supplier that provides it.

column_meanings.meaning: Unique identifier for each product
Descriptive name of the product
Broad grouping of the product (e.g., beauty, toys, home_goods, sports)
Standard selling price of the product
Current availability status of the product (e.g., active, discontinued, out_of_stock)
Identifier of the supplier that provides this product

tables.business_value: Enables product portfolio analysis, pricing strategy, and supplier performance tracking.

ambiguity_flags.note: status here reflects product availability. Other tables (returns, suppliers, marketing_campaigns, customers, orders) also have a status column with unrelated meanings; no declared link indicates a generic use of the term.
price is a monetary figure, but the currency is not indicated in the sample.
